svg.text: One key block in v0, line by line (lines 1–4)
The block's 128 threads (4 warps) run these lines once per key block j: 64 keys of K and their 64 rows of V. Each panel takes one line.
Blue: thread 0 (lane 0 of warp 0) and its values. Inside the k loop the figure shows k = 1, head dims 16–31.

block j − 1: S, softmax, O += P V
block j − 1: S, softmax, O += P V
block j − 1: S, softmax, O += P V
block j − 1: S, softmax, O += P V
Without the barrier, warp 2 would start overwriting sK and sV here,
while warp 3 is still reading block j − 1's V for O += P V.
Shared memory has room for one key block of K (sK) and one
of V (sV). Every key block reuses the same spots, so block
j can only be written once nobody needs block j − 1.
The 4 warps reach this line at different times.
sync_threads holds each of the 128 threads here until all

svg.text: # LDG, then STS, for K and V
Blue: thread 0's 4 pieces, 16 bytes each: rows 0, 16, 32, 48, values 0–7.
All 128 threads at once: 512 pieces × 16 bytes = 8 KB, the whole tile.
tKgK[None, None, None, j] picks key block j; g2s gives
each thread 4 pieces of it (the copy figure in idea 4
Its atom, CopyUniversalOp, is a plain copy, so each piece
makes two trips: a global load (LDG) into the thread's
The store waits for its load, a trip to global memory of
hundreds of cycles, and ④ then waits for every store.
Round 4's cp.async skips the registers and lets the copy
The same copy for V: the values of the same 64 keys

svg.text: tVgV and tVsV come from the same g2s, so thread 0 copies
the same spots of V: rows 0, 16, 32, 48, values 0–7.
Row r of V belongs to the same key as row r of K. S = Q Kᵀ
scores the 64 keys of block j; O += P V then mixes their
64 rows of V. Both have to sit in shared memory together.
The real kernel interleaves the two copies, one step of K
then one of V. Nothing reads either until ④, so the order

svg.text: # K, V are in shared memory
sK: who wrote each row, and what thread 0 reads
read by thread 0 in the k loop
In ② and ③ each thread wrote 8 small pieces. The k loop
reads sK in a different pattern, the tiled MMA's: thread 0
Half of those rows were written by warp 2 (threads 64–71),
which may still be copying. The same holds for V in O += P
V. So every thread waits here until all 128 have finished
② and ③: a second BAR.SYNC, two per key block.
